results.snippet:
# European e-bike market: 2025 in review

Unit volumes across the European Union settled at approximately 7.0 million e-bikes in
2025, against 5.0 million in 2022. Growth has decelerated markedly from the 2021 peak
and the market is now best described as mature in the western member states and still
expanding in central and eastern Europe.

results.title: European bicycle market — first quarter 2026 commentary
results.snippet:
# European bicycle market, Q1 2026

The first quarter opened weakly across most western European markets, with unit volumes
down modestly against a strong comparative period. Cargo formats continued to outgrow
the market as a whole.

Currency movement was a live factor for operators selling into the United Kingdom. The
euro strengthened against sterling through the quarter, which compresses the euro value
of a sterling-denominated sale unless the retail price is repriced.

results.title: Cycle-count clauses in e-bike battery warranties
results.snippet:
# Cycle-count clauses in battery warranties

A cycle-count clause caps a battery warranty by charge cycles as well as by elapsed
time, on whichever limit is reached first. Clauses in the 500 to 800 cycle range are
now common on packs above 600 Wh.

The commercial logic is that calendar ageing and cycle ageing are different failure
modes, and a heavy-use commercial rider can exhaust a pack's cycle life well inside a
24-month calendar window.

Enforcement depends entirely on whether the battery management system reco

results.title: Velora — warranty registry, scope note
results.snippet:
# Warranty registry — scope note

The warranty registry records the warranty status of a serialised product against its
order. It covers bicycles from model year 2024 onward.

Fields recorded are: serial number, order reference, registration date, warranty class
and expiry. Cycle counts are NOT recorded in the registry; where a cycle-count clause
applies, the count must be read from the battery management system at the point of
claim.

Accessories are not serialised and are therefore not represented in the registry

results.title: Direct-to-consumer logistics cost benchmarks
results.snippet:
# Logistics cost benchmarks for direct-to-consumer bicycle retail

Outbound carriage on a boxed bicycle within continental Europe benchmarks at EUR 38 to
EUR 62 depending on lane and volume commitment. Island and peripheral destinations sit
materially above that band.

Inbound freight on containerised bicycle imports benchmarks at EUR 40 to EUR 55 per
unit on the standard sea-plus-road route at typical container fill rates.

Accessories move at a fraction of that: EUR 3 to EUR 6 per unit inbound on the same
lanes,

results.snippet:
# Cycle-count clauses in battery warranties

A cycle-count clause caps a battery warranty by charge cycles as well as by elapsed
time, on whichever limit is reached first. Clauses in the 500 to 800 cycle range are
now common on packs above 600 Wh.

The commercial logic is that calendar ageing and cycle ageing are different failure
modes, and a heavy-use commercial rider can exhaust a pack's cycle life well inside a
24-month calendar window.

results.snippet:
# Warranty registry — scope note

The warranty registry records the warranty status of a serialised product against its
order. It covers bicycles from model year 2024 onward.

Fields recorded are: serial number, order reference, registration date, warranty class
and expiry. Cycle counts are NOT recorded in the registry; where a cycle-count clause
applies, the count must be read from the battery management system at the point of
claim.

Accessories are not serialised and are therefore not represented in the registry
